title: AusSuper will admit to death benefit bungles
full_text:
AustralianSuper will settle with the corporate regulator and admit it broke financial services laws when it failed to pay out thousands of death benefit claims to families of deceased members in a timely manner.
Two sources with knowledge of the issue, who commented anonymously to discuss matters that are before the court, said the $410 billion pension giant and the Australian Securities and Investments Commission were in the final stages of sketching out the agreed facts to be lodged with the Federal Court on Monday.
The exact allegations to which AustralianSuper will admit, and what penalties will apply, have not yet been made public.
ASIC secured a $23.5 million fine from the Wayne Swan-chaired Cbus over similar failures in November 2025.
AustralianSuper and ASIC declined to comment.
The matter is scheduled for a hearing on September 9 before Federal Court Justice David O'Callaghan.
A settlement will bring to an end an 18-month legal battle between the fund and the regulator, which alleged that AustralianSuper left bereaved families waiting for their deceased loved one's leftover retirement savings and insurance benefits for an unreasonably long time between 2019 and 2024.
ASIC cited nearly 7000 cases where families were left waiting from four months to four years for payment.
Superannuation laws require a fund pay out a death benefit "as soon as practicable", and delays and poor practice in this area have been a focus for the corporate watchdog as it zeroes in on member service issues in the sector.
